Interface ConfigurationWatchRequest

public interface ConfigurationWatchRequest
A request to watch the configuration, all of it or under a prefix, started with WatchableBeanContext.configuration() or WatchableBeanContext.configuration(String), and completed by watch(ConfigurationWatcher) or watchReloading(ReloadingConfigurationWatcher). The watcher is called, after the configuration beans under the prefix were bound again, for every refresh that touches the prefix. 
context.configuration("datasources.default")
    .withFirstBatch()
    .watch(change -> pool.resize(configuration.getMaximumPoolSize()));

Which watcher

  • watch(ConfigurationWatcher) takes a ConfigurationWatcher, which returns nothing: the watcher applies every change to the live bean, and the refresh reports it as ReloadingConfigurationWatcher.Outcome.APPLIED. This is the common case, such as a pool that resizes.
  • watchReloading(ReloadingConfigurationWatcher) takes a ReloadingConfigurationWatcher, which answers an ReloadingConfigurationWatcher.Outcome per change: for a watcher that cannot always apply a change in place, and asks for its bean to be recreated, or for a restart.

The two are one kind of watch: a plain watcher is called as a reloading one that always answers APPLIED, and both are ordered, delivered and closed alike.

A watch registered while a bean is being created belongs to that bean, which is what lets a reloading watcher answer ReloadingConfigurationWatcher.Outcome.RECREATE. Each terminal operation takes a snapshot of the request, so a request may be reused for further watches.

  • Method Details

    • withFirstBatch

      ConfigurationWatchRequest withFirstBatch()
      Starts the watch with a first batch, as the other watches always do: the watcher is called once as it is registered, or as the context starts when it has not started yet, with a change whose ConfigurationChange.initial() holds, to read the configuration as it is then. Every refresh after that read reaches the watcher, which a read of its own before registering cannot promise. Without it, the watcher is called for the refreshes only.
      Returns:
      This request

    • watch

      BeanWatch watch(ConfigurationWatcher watcher)
      Registers a watcher that applies every change it is given.
      Parameters:
      watcher - The watcher
      Returns:
      The watch, to close when the changes are no longer needed

    • watchReloading

      BeanWatch watchReloading(ReloadingConfigurationWatcher watcher)
      Registers a watcher that says what it did with each change, such as a bean that must be recreated, or a server that must be restarted for a change to apply. It is named apart from watch(ConfigurationWatcher) so that a lambda is not ambiguous between the two.
      Parameters:
      watcher - The watcher
      Returns:
      The watch, to close when the changes are no longer needed
